title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. The vehicle did not slow down or stop after the incident, according to a resident's report. This represents a failure in object detection and response, where the autonomous system did not recognize a small animal in its path or initiate appropriate evasive or stopping behavior.

The system was deployed in a neighborhood setting with pedestrians and wildlife present. A human safety operator was in the vehicle but did not intervene to prevent the collision. It is not established whether the operator could have prevented the outcome, or what the detection and response capabilities of the system were designed to handle.

Avride disputed that the vehicle failed to stop at intersections, though this does not address whether the system detected the duck or attempted to avoid it. The company subsequently excluded certain streets from its service area and stated it would conduct simulated experiments to improve performance. Whether these changes will address small-animal detection is not established.

Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood, causing significant community backlash. The duck, which residents knew well as it nested outside a local Italian restaurant, was hit by the self-driving car while operating in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present. A resident reported on social media that the vehicle did not slow down or stop after the incident. Residents have since placed the duck's eggs in an incubator to preserve them.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was in autonomous mode but disputed claims that it failed to stop at a stop sign, stating it made complete and appropriate stops at all relevant intersections. The company has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake from its service area. Avride is now conducting simulated experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar situations, while ensuring any changes do not compromise safety performance. Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo, Zoox, and Tesla, also operate in Austin.
